about: Time range limits parity cases, read by tests/unit_tests/utils/test_date_range_parity.py (server) and dateRangeParity.test.ts (browser). Each case gives the policy levels in level order (global, dataset, dashboard), the server's now, and the resolved since/until (what /api/v1/time_range/ returns), all naive server wall-clock times. zone is a label for the reader only: neither side takes a zone. expected.outcome is pass, no_limits, invalid_policy, since_after_until or failure (the first broken rule). A tie case gives the dashboard payload (global, dashboard, datasets) instead of levels: the browser builds its levels with dashboardLimitLevels, the server orders them as get_effective_time_range_limits does.
